overview.text: The Checkered Keelback, or Asiatic Water Snake, is a very common non-venomous water snake of South and South-east Asia.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: From Afghanistan and Pakistan through India, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh to Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, southern China and Malaysia.

habitat.text: In or near fresh water and rice paddies; active by day and by night.

behaviour.text: If cornered it rears up and spreads its neck skin like a cobra's hood. It is not venomous, but its bite is painful. It can even lose part of its tail to escape.

diet.text: Mainly fish, frogs and arthropods; sometimes rodents and frog eggs.

reproduction.text: Usually lays 30 to 70 eggs (from 4 to 100). The female guards them until they hatch after 60 to 70 days; hatchlings are about 11 cm long.

recognise.text: Usually in or near water or rice paddies.
May spread its neck like a cobra when cornered.
